parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is classed as domain because of its `*.entity.ts` pattern, but everything in it is persistence (infrastructure) work. `CustomBaseEntity` extends TypeORM's `BaseEntity`, which is the Active Record pattern. That gives every subclass (UserEntity, RoleEntity, PermissionEntity, EmailTemplateEntity) persistence methods such as save, remove and find. The class body only maps fields to the database: an auto-generated primary key, and timestamp columns with SQL defaults (`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`) and `onUpdate` triggers. The file has no domain behaviour, invariants or business concepts. It is an ORM schema/Active Record base class, which is infrastructure-kind work sitting in the domain layer. Confidence is moderate because putting ORM decorators on entities is common in NestJS projects. Still, inheriting Active Record persistence and declaring SQL column settings clearly goes beyond what a domain unit should do.

violations.message: CustomBaseEntity extends TypeORM BaseEntity (Active Record), so it carries persistence operations (save/remove/find). Its members are only ORM/database schema mappings (@PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @CreateDateColumn/@UpdateDateColumn with SQL timestamp defaults and onUpdate). That is persistence responsibility, which belongs to the infrastructure layer, not domain.
